title: Functional training doesn't exist
summary: He argues 'functional training' is a myth: the moves labelled functional (pull-ups, crawls, pistols, rope climbs, sprints) rarely show up in daily life, while squats, deadlifts and curls do. He thinks most functional and calisthenics trainees are closet bodybuilders who train for looks but won't say so, and that the do-everything approach gives mediocre results. Every lift is functional for some goal, and for bodybuilding that goal is hypertrophy.
claims: There is no such thing as functional training; people who think they train functionally are deluded, and it hurts them and fitness in general
If functional training really copied daily movements it would be things like lifting bags or opening car doors; instead it picks movements like crawling and rope climbing that people rarely do
He agrees humans should keep a full range of motion even if those motions aren't used daily
Pull-ups are among the least functional lifts: almost nobody uses a vertical pull in daily life, and firefighters need about one rep to climb in a window
Climbing a wall isn't a strict pull-up; your center of gravity is behind you, so a cheated one-arm-then-the-other muscle-up is closer to real climbing
Weighted pull-ups with a belt and plates have no real-life equivalent, so by functional logic adding load makes the lift non-functional
By daily-use logic, squats and deadlifts (knee flexion and hip hinge) and even curls are more functional than pull-ups
Front raises copy a common daily motion, while pistols, shrimp squats and single-arm or single-leg calisthenics look cool but aren't functional
If a skill like a pull-up is truly functional, once you can do one you are set for life, so progressing it isn't needed for function
'Commando' functional trainees doing bear crawls with weighted vests and chains are LARPing as soldiers
A French military trainer in Guiana admitted jungle drills are mostly about toughening men up, not direct application
Soldiers and athletes who train for a real application never call it 'functional training'; they call it training or sport-specific training
An office worker would gain more from strengthening the lower back and fixing posture; a blue-collar worker's job is already functional, so plain strength training suits them
Athlean-X sells athletic functional training, but he trains to be lean and aesthetic and coaches of real athletes see him as a hack
Athleticism is not a look: a six-pack has nothing to do with being athletic, and most real athletes carry body fat
He has a great six-pack yet can barely run or jump, and is less athletic than many people who look worse
Andy Ruiz, the 'fat' boxer, beat the bodybuilder-looking Anthony Joshua in their first fight, showing function isn't tied to looks
The 'sumo test': if someone says a sumo wrestler isn't athletic, they judge athleticism only by appearance
No exercise is functional overall; low body fat is functional for calisthenics athletes' sport, not in general
Many functional and calisthenics trainees are closet bodybuilders who train for looks but hide it because training for looks is stigmatised as vain or feminine
Twist on Ronnie Coleman: everyone wants to look like a bodybuilder but not everyone wants to admit being one
Jacked athletes who claim they 'don't lift' usually do dumbbell and cable work and just don't count it
Football teammates who claimed to be naturally big actually trained more than anyone, some since age 13 for 5-6 hours a week, and hid it to look genetically gifted
Sprints are functional only for getting faster at sprinting
'Fitness YouTube' is really lifter YouTube; bodybuilders and powerlifters share the same means and differ only in goals
Most people lift primarily for aesthetics, and that is perfectly fine; you don't need to justify it with mobility or old-age excuses
You don't need a productive justification for training; 'because I want to look good' is enough
Training is an escape from your day job (he programs 10 hours a day at a desk), so by definition it isn't functional to your daily motions
No program builds strength and size equally without trading one for the other; a program that makes you very strong costs some hypertrophy
Chase two rabbits and you catch neither: a boxer never tries to get as big as possible because it would hurt his boxing
Most people do CrossFit or powerbuilding to look better, and most powerbuilders end up as poor powerlifters and poor bodybuilders
Every lift is functional for something; curls are functional for hypertrophy, and resistance training was made to isolate the muscle-growing part of physical work
The Bioneer is respected but popular because he is jacked; his videos like 'lats like Bruce Lee' are really aesthetic content, and his programs are subpar for bodybuilding
Middle-aged men using functional training to relive high-school sports glory are not athletes unless they compete
Ido Portal openly dislikes bodybuilding and training for looks yet is shirtless in almost all his videos
Calisthenics moves aren't more natural than weighted ones; any motion the body can do (deadlift, curl) is natural
There are no 'fake muscles' from weights versus 'real muscles' from calisthenics; all training is resistance training
